pr_title: Update BoundedMemory.Unix to set up poison around the memory
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/40846

Marking as draft as I haven't verified if it actually works yet. Plus, most of the code is the same as the Windows version of the code with some Unix-specific tweaks; There might be places where we might be able to simplify some of the code.

issue_context.title: BoundedMemory test helper needs an implementation on non-Windows platforms
issue_context.body:
Our test infrastructure has a type `BoundedMemory` that's used for unit-testing unsafe code. The helper sets up poison (NOACCESS) pages around a `Span<T>` so that out-of-bounds accesses are discovered during testing.

This type [has a working implementation](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/tests/TestUtilities/System/Buffers/BoundedMemory.Windows.cs) on Windows, but the non-Windows implementation falls back to using [standard arrays without NOACCESS buffers](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/tests/TestUtilities/System/Buffers/BoundedMemory.Unix.cs).

We should bring the UNIX implementation up to par with the Windows implementation so that tests running in non-Windows environments get the same checks that tests running in Windows environments get.

Looks like we might be able to use `mmap`[1](#f1)and `mprotect` to achieve something similar. Most of the logics seem similar enough so I could give this a go, if nobody is already working on it. (although admittedly I lack experiences with Unix) 1 "POSIX says that the behavior of mprotect() is unspecified if it is applied to a region of memory that was not obtained via mmap(2)." (man-pages, Release 5.05, mprotect(2)) [↩](#a1)

Looks like https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/105595 added more capabilities to the Unix implementation. It looks like it only needs a little more work in the `MakeReadonly` and `MakeWriteable` methods.

review_comments: Why can't this just use MemoryMappedFile.CreateNew rather than direct use of mmap?

1. I didn't realise that thing existed (😅)
2. I'm just not sure how portable that would be - we'll be basically relying on MemoryMappedFile using some function that works with `mprotect`, and the only thing I know about it is that only mappings that have been created through `mmap` are 'guaranteed' to work ("POSIX says that the behavior of mprotect() is unspecified if it is applied to a region of memory that was not obtained via mmap(2)." (man-pages, Release 5.05, mprotect(2)).
While I see that things should "just work" with any memory (e.g. even the example in `man mprotect` uses `memalign` to allocate the memory) I wasn't sure if there's certain distros / etc that didn't support it - I lack experiences with *Nix stuffs in general. So I just went with the naive approach of P/Invoking `mmap` directly from the C# code.

Looks like the current implementation uses `shm_open`, perhaps `HAVE_SHM_OPEN_THAT_WORKS_WELL_ENOUGH_WITH_MMAP` variable means it's somewhat of an equivalent and should also work with `mprotect`?
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c00478bb92a8eae42bf720ebd1b0bad81a34f5a4/src/libraries/Native/Unix/System.Native/pal_io.c#L311-L313

If it works and you think it's okay to use it, I'd be more than happy to use that instead. Would definitely help cleaning up this mess...

> I'm just not sure how portable that would be

Much more portable than this manual managed implementation ;-)
Currently I have some problems running WSL (recent Insider Preview builds broke it) so I won't be able to verify the change until I set up another VM with Linux on it, but I certainly could try that.
